argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only in a narrowed, caveated form. Aggregate readiness clears threshold and the launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports release readiness at the overall level. Public governance guidance also supports deployment when current evaluation results, limitations, and ongoing monitoring are documented. The limiting fact is the developer-support migration regression: it is a live material segment weakness for a named launch use case, and the current record does not show approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance. On this record, the defensible position is not that compliance is already fully proved, but that certification can be treated as caveated only if the certification package is understood to require explicit disclosure of that weakness in the current release documentation at certification time.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue on the admissible record.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not let prior approval or an informal monitoring comment substitute for current-release evidence. The policy question is narrower: whether certification may proceed when the current record shows aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but also shows a material segment weakness with no approved mitigation. The best reading of the policy-consistent path is caveated compliance tied to current-release disclosure of the weakness alongside current evaluation results. The admissible evidence supports that disclosure is required; it does not support claiming that disclosure has already been demonstrated on the present record.
concessions: The current record does not prove that the required disclosure already exists in current release documentation.
The developer-support migration slice is below the warning threshold and regressed relative to the prior approved release.
The release thread contains only an informal monitoring comment and does not show reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or approved risk acceptance.
Prior approval is contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
